Affected baseline items: 14 of 18—Although; boneless bites; chicken tenders; french fries; fried dough; Gluten-Free Cauliflower Crust; many salad dressings; mozzarella sticks; pizza logs; pizzas; tenders; The Half-Baked; the truncated fryer sentence; and wing sauces. Reconciliation covered all 18 keys exactly once: 2 artifact/not_applicable, 5 exact_match/verified, 10 normalized_match/accurately_unavailable, and 1 exact_match/accurately_unavailable.
The official specials page is a current restaurant-issued surface omitted upstream; it lists everyday combinations, daily promotions, and weekday lunch specials.
The linked Falls Church Toast catalog includes alcoholic beverages omitted from Luna's nonalcoholic-beverage grouping and includes current Hot Honey Pepperoni presentations.

The allergen page is blocked on direct reopening but its indexed restaurant-issued content is detailed enough to preserve explicit positive evidence. It is not a complete item-level allergen matrix and cannot establish negatives or complete arrays.
The cauliflower-crust warning supports wheat/gluten cross-contact only, while its ingredient list explicitly supports milk and egg as contains allergens.
The official page's general kitchen disclaimer and fryer warning support cross-contact risk; they do not justify complete allergen arrays or absence claims.
The baseline rows named “Although” and the truncated fryer sentence are prose-extraction artifacts rather than products.

Rejected Terra's blanket treatment of the six named fried products as having only may-contain wheat/gluten. The restaurant explicitly calls fried dough, chicken tenders, boneless bites, mozzarella sticks, pizza logs, and french fries items “that contain gluten”; the subsequent fryer language adds cross-contact risk but does not erase that positive.

Rejected Terra's accurately_unavailable reconciliation for boneless bites and tenders insofar as it demotes soy entirely to may-contain. The restaurant explicitly identifies soy/soybean oil as ingredients in its tenders/bites, supporting narrow contains-soy evidence without implying a complete array.

Rejected any interpretation that incomplete allergen coverage erases unavoidable named-identity positives. For example, mozzarella sticks support milk as a narrow positive, while still lacking a complete allergen array.

Rejected Terra's unavailable-allergen treatment for Hot Honey Pepperoni insofar as the restaurant-linked description explicitly names cheese; that supports at least a narrow milk positive, not a complete array.
